changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail store-operations buyers, headline with the customer's words: 'One system for the tills and the website.' Replace the abstract claim with a live, step-by-step demo of an online order returned at a store till: refunded to the original payment and credited to the same customer's loyalty profile. Say 'tills', not 'point of sale' or 'in-person payments'.
changes.why: The head of store operations dismissed M3 as 'that's a diagram.' and asked how a return works step by step at the till; we 'described it' but 'never showed it', while she had already used the sharper phrase 'One system for the tills and the website.'

changes.change: For COO and store-ops buyers, add an accountability line and proof point: one contract and one escalation path for the tills and the website, naming who installs, who runs the rollout and who answers a till outage. Support it with a template rollout plan covering dates, who installs and what happens to the old tills. Answer the fear directly: 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.'
changes.why: Our answer that a partner would do installs ended Bev's questions. Adyen pitched one platform 'on one contract' with people who had done store rollouts, and the store team asked for a rollout plan covering 'who installs'.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail store teams, offer callable references instead of customer stories: named retailers who have rolled out our tills, with a call set up before the stores workshop.
changes.why: The buyer asked 'can I talk to them?' and we couldn't set up a call in time, while the competitor named retailers Angela knew.

changes.change: For retailers selling in stores and online, add a retail opener built on the store-floor problem: an online order the store can't see, so staff refund to gift cards or tell people to mail it back, and a loyalty program that fails because store and web hold two different customer records. Position the answer as 'one customer, one basket'.
changes.why: The evaluation was triggered by store returns and a split loyalty record, and the customer framed the goal as 'one customer, one basket'. We led instead with online checkout, which was not why they were buying.
